# F9 · Chip proposal — Wildcard and Free Hit

*Extracted verbatim from the PRD, which remains the single source of truth for every criterion below. Edit the PRD, then regenerate — never edit this file.*

Identifiers in this file: `F9-AC-01` – `F9-UP-02`.

#### F9 · Chip proposal — Wildcard and Free Hit

| Section | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Priority | **Could.** A full squad rebuild is the least frequently used flow of the nine features — chips are played a handful of times a season — so the most defensible to slip if the schedule tightens. |
| Serves | The same anchor as F5 — the first core job's chip decision (Section 2.3) — specifically the two chips that require a full squad rebuild rather than a weekly review. |
| Happy path | From the Chips tab (F5), a *Generate proposal* control on the Wildcard or Free Hit row opens this screen: a summary card, a verdict, and the proposed fifteen grouped by position. The manager locks players they want kept and regenerates the rest, as many times as they like, then leaves — there is nothing to confirm or apply here. |
| **Acceptance Criteria** |  |
| **F9-AC-01** | Only Wildcard and Free Hit carry the *Generate proposal* control. A spent chip's row shows no control at all, consistent with F5's spent-chip state. |
| **F9-AC-02** | **The header states which chip the proposal is for and the horizon it is built across** — Wildcard over several gameweeks ("Built for GW9 → GW14"), Free Hit this week only and reverting after ("This week only · GW4"). |
| **F9-AC-03** | The two chips are otherwise visually identical: the permanent-versus-reverting difference is carried entirely by that horizon text, never by a badge or icon. |
| **F9-AC-04** | **A summary card gives three figures at a glance:** the signed xPts delta against the current eleven, the money left from the squad value this proposal spends, and a count of changes ("4 changes"). |
| **F9-AC-05** | The money figure here is chip-local — not the NBal of 3.1 — because a chip week is a rebuild rather than a set of costed swaps. |
| **F9-AC-06** | Below the figures, an aim line in the assistant's voice states the proposal's intent — for example *"Five repairs, not a rebuild: Muñoz out, Wood out, Mbeumo → Gibbs-White on the same money, and two bench slots that actually start. Ten of the fifteen stay."* |
| **F9-AC-07** | After a regeneration, the aim line reports what the regeneration did — how many slots moved, and that locked players and their prices are untouched — rather than repeating the original aim. |
| **F9-AC-08** | **A verdict strip restates F5's verdict vocabulary** (play, target, hold, spent) for this one chip, plus a one-line reason. |
| **F9-AC-09** | Once ten or more of the fifteen are locked, the verdict is overridden to *not worth it* — at that point the chip is doing the work of two or three ordinary transfers. The badge's colour does not change between states; only its text and reason line do. |
| **F9-AC-10** | The list header carries a *Collapse all* control alongside the fifteen player rows. |
| **F9-AC-11** | The fifteen are grouped by position in a fixed order — goalkeepers, defenders, midfielders, forwards — the same grouping as the Squad screen (F1). |
| **F9-AC-12** | **Each row shows the player, an In or Kept tag, a Lock control, and a collapsed one-line reason.** *In* means a genuine change from the current squad; *Kept* means unchanged. |
| **F9-AC-13** | A row's reason expands on tap and never by default — fifteen reasons expanded is a wall, fifteen names is a squad. |
| **F9-AC-14** | Locking a player is reflected immediately in that row's own visual state and excludes the slot from the next regeneration. |
| **F9-AC-15** | There is no cap on how many of the fifteen can be locked. Locking all fifteen is legal; it leaves nothing for *Generate again* to change. |
| **F9-AC-16** | **A footer is always present**, carrying a **Generate again** control, how many slots are free to change, and how much money is left. |
| **F9-AC-17** | The footer also carries a persistent hint — *"Tap lock to keep a player through the next generation"* before any lock, or *"N player(s) locked · generate again moves the rest"* once at least one is. |
| **F9-AC-18** | **The money-left figure in the summary card and the one in the footer are the same number, computed once.** Two independently derived versions of one figure that can disagree is a defect, not a design choice — the rule already stated for the conviction engine (3.2) and the squad totals (F1-AC-22) applies here. |
| **F9-AC-19** | **This screen has no confirm, apply or play action, and none is planned.** It is advice only, exactly like the season plan it is reached from (F5): the manager reviews the fifteen and, if he chooses to, plays the chip in the FPL app himself. Nothing here marks a chip as played or writes to FPL (2.5; Reliability NFR). |
| **F9-AC-20** | The only ways to leave this screen are back — which discards every lock and swap, since nothing here was ever saved — and *Generate again*. |
| **F9-AC-21** | **In v1 scope, not shipped as a demonstration:** regeneration draws from real candidate alternates for every unlocked slot, not a fixed placeholder set for a handful of positions. |
| **F9-AC-22** | The proposed fifteen is validated against FPL's rules before it is shown (see Unhappy Paths). |
| **F9-AC-23** | Locks and any in-progress swaps are namespaced per chip: opening a Free Hit proposal never shows the Wildcard's locks. |
| **F9-AC-24** | In a Wildcard or Free Hit week the weekly transfer queue (F3) is not used at all — that week is a squad build, not a swap queue. |
| **Unhappy Paths** |  |
| **F9-UP-01** | **The proposed fifteen breaks an FPL rule.** Acceptance: the *scenario cannot be entered* state names the breach with its numbers; the squad must be validated against FPL's rules — fifteen players, two/five/five/three by position, maximum three per club, within budget — before it is shown. Automatic resolution is out of scope. |
| **F9-UP-02** | **The manager leaves without locking or changing anything.** Acceptance: legitimate, and the default case — nothing on this screen is ever saved, so there is no unsaved-changes warning to show. |
